Chess Openings Glossary

Terms you'll hear at the board, minus the intimidation.

Opening Ideas

  • Gambit — Sacrifice material (usually a pawn) for faster development or an attack. Bold, sometimes reckless.
  • Tempo — A unit of time measured in moves. Gaining tempo means developing while threatening something.
  • Development — Getting your pieces off the back rank and into useful squares.
  • Castling — The one move where king and rook swap. Tucks the king safe and activates the rook.
  • En passant — A pawn can capture an adjacent pawn that just moved two squares, as if it moved one.
  • Fianchetto — Developing a bishop to the long diagonal, often behind a knight pawn.

Common Openings

  • Sicilian Defense — 1.e4 c5. Black fights for the center asymmetrically. Sharp and popular.
  • Ruy Lopez — 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5. Spanish opening. Rich in strategy.
  • Queen's Gambit — 1.d4 d5 2.c4. Not a true gambit; the pawn is usually regained.
Tip: Don't memorize lines before you understand the ideas. Openings are conversations, not scripts.

Key Terms

The height of the strings above the frets. Lower action feels faster but can buzz; higher is cleaner but stiffer.

A slight forward bow in the neck. A little relief keeps strings from rattling against the frets.

Whether the guitar plays in tune up and down the neck. Adjusted by moving the saddles.

Cassette is the stack of gears at the back wheel. Chainring is the toothed disc at the pedals, front. Chain crosses both.
Indexing
Tuning the shifter so each click lands the chain dead centre on a cog. Cable tension is the adjustment; a quarter turn goes a long way.
Chain Wear (Stretch)
Pins and plates wear, so the chain grows. A worn chain eats cassettes. Check with a gauge every few hundred miles.
Truing a Wheel
Straightening side-to-side wobble by turning spoke nipples. Tiny turns, quarter at a time, and check as you go.
Bottom Bracket
The bearing set inside the frame that the cranks spin on. Creaks from here sound like they come from everywhere else.
A skipping chain on one cog only is usually a bent tooth or a stiff link, not a shifting problem. Look before you twist.

Home Networking Glossary

For user_name, and anyone who has rebooted a router today.

IP Address
A device's number on the network. 192.168.x.x is the usual home range; the router hands them out and keeps a list.
DHCP
The automatic address desk. It leases your laptop an IP for a while and takes it back when you leave.
DNS
The phone book from names to numbers — example.com becomes an IP. Slow DNS feels like slow internet even when speed tests look fine.
Subnet Mask
Says which part of an IP is the street and which is the house number. 255.255.255.0 means the first three chunks are the street.
NAT
The router's trick of sharing one public address among all your devices. It's why outside machines can't knock on your door uninvited.
VPN
A private tunnel between you and somewhere else. It hides traffic from the local network and shifts where you appear to be.
Band: 2.4 GHz vs 5 GHz
2.4 travels further through walls but is busier and slower. 5 is faster and fussier about distance.
Slow Wi-Fi in one room? Move the router off the floor, away from the microwave, and try the 5 GHz band if you're close.

Beekeeping Glossary

Hive vocabulary for user_name. The bees know it already.

Brood
Developing bees, egg to pupa, in the wax cells. Flat capped brood is workers; domed caps are drones.
Super
A box stacked above the brood chamber, usually just for honey. Remove the queen excluder debate at your own risk.
Queen Excluder
A slotted grid the queen can't pass, keeping brood out of honey supers. Workers slip through easily.
Swarming
The colony splits: old queen leaves with half the bees. Signs are queen cells along the comb edges. Manage it or catch it.
Robbing
Bees from another hive stealing your stores, often in a dearth. Keep entrances small and don't spill syrup around.
Propolis
Plant-resin glue the bees make. Sticky, antimicrobial, and the reason your hive tool exists.
Smoker
Cool white smoke masks alarm pheromone and settles the colony. Puff gently; you're calming, not fumigating.
A hive that suddenly feels light in a dearth is being robbed. Shrink the entrance tonight, not next weekend.
